title: Given an array of positive integers and a target value, find the length of the shortest contiguous subarray whose sum is greater than or equal to the target, returning zero if no such subarray exists. Solve it with the sliding window pattern and demonstrate with a complete banking mini-project.
shortTitle: Minimum Size Subarray Sum (Shortest Subarray with Sum At Least Target)
keyPoints: Grow the right pointer to add elements until the sum reaches the target.
Shrink from the left while the sum stays at or above the target, tracking the shortest window.
Correctness depends entirely on all elements being positive, which makes the sum monotonic.
If negatives are present, this simple window breaks and a prefix-sum plus monotonic deque is needed.
Time complexity is O(N) because both pointers only move forward; space is O(1).
Initialize best length to a sentinel and return zero if no qualifying window is found.

s1_definition.oneliner: Grow right until the sum reaches the target, then shrink left while it still qualifies, tracking the shortest window.
s1_definition.profdef:
- This problem asks for the **smallest length** of a contiguous subarray whose sum is at least a target.
- All elements are **positive**, which makes the running sum monotonically increase as the window grows.
- A **variable-size sliding window** grows right and shrinks left aggressively while the sum qualifies.
- The shrink-while-valid pattern finds the shortest qualifying window ending at each position.
- Time is **O(N)** and space is **O(1)**.
- If negatives are present, a **prefix-sum plus monotonic deque** is required instead.
s1_definition.analogy: At the National Bank of India, Rajesh reviews a sequence of daily deposit amounts into Priya's current account and wants the fewest consecutive days needed to accumulate at least a target amount for a liquidity certificate. He slides a window: he adds days on the right until the total reaches the target, then trims days off the left as long as he still meets the target, always remembering the shortest qualifying span.

sections.s6_takeaway:
This problem asks for the shortest contiguous subarray whose sum reaches at least a target, where all elements are positive, and you solve it with a variable-size sliding window in linear time. The right pointer advances and adds each element to a running sum. Whenever the sum reaches the target, the window qualifies, so you record its length and greedily shrink from the left while the sum stays at or above the target, which finds the shortest qualifying window ending at the current position.

The correctness of the greedy shrink depends entirely on all elements being positive. Positivity makes the sum monotonically increase as the window grows and decrease as it shrinks. If the array could contain negatives, the window would break and you would need a prefix-sum array combined with a monotonic deque.

At the National Bank of India, Rajesh used this on the treasury desk to certify corporate accounts. The team reviewed a sequence of daily net inflows and needed the shortest run of consecutive days during which the account accumulated at least a regulatory liquidity threshold. Each inflow was positive, so the greedy window applied directly, and the linear pass scaled across the bank's large corporate customer base.

The senior-level point is that this is the shrink-aggressively variant of the sliding window, the mirror image of problems where you grow aggressively. Knowing which direction to be greedy in, and knowing that the greedy shrink fails the moment negatives appear, is the real depth signal.

Remember one sentence: grow right until the sum reaches the target, then shrink left while it still qualifies, and the shortest qualifying window is the answer.
